answers.reasoning: The lesson says the store exposes four methods - setState, getState, getInitialState, subscribe - and nothing else, matching the api object literal shown.
The bail-out compares the raw partial (nextState) to state by reference before any merge, and a fresh {value:1} object is never Object.is the current state, so the listener still runs.
The lesson's own worked example says the merge is one level deep and the OLD nested object is entirely replaced, so label is dropped while other survives, giving {nested:{count:1},other:5}.
The lesson states that omitting replace when next is null causes a direct assign with no merge, so setState(null) with no second argument sets state to exactly null.
getInitialState just returns the closure variable initialState, which was set once when the state creator ran and is never touched by setState, so it stays the same original object reference.
